title: Lead-Time Multiplier for Rush Alterations Against the Needed-By Date (Marlowe & Finch Alterations)
content:
For rush work at Marlowe & Finch Alterations, a lead-time multiplier applies to the rush charge basis, read from the calendar days between the ticket's drop-off date and its needed-by date (the event date recorded on the ticket).

| Calendar days from drop-off date to needed-by date | Lead-time multiplier |
|---|---|
| 7 days or fewer | 150 percent |
| 8 to 14 days | 125 percent |
| 15 days or more | 100 percent |
| No needed-by date on the ticket | 100 percent |

**Counting.** The days are the calendar days between the two dates on the ticket: a needed-by date one day after the drop-off date is 1 day; the drop-off date itself is not counted as a day.

## Boundaries on both sides

| Days | Band | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 7 days or fewer | 150 percent |
| 8 | 8 to 14 days | 125 percent |
| 14 | 8 to 14 days | 125 percent |
| 15 | 15 days or more | 100 percent |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- Drop-off on the 3rd of a month, needed-by date on the 13th of the same month: 10 days, multiplier 125 percent.
- Drop-off on the 28th of a 30-day month, needed-by date on the 2nd of the next month: 4 days, multiplier 150 percent.
- A ticket that records no needed-by date: multiplier 100 percent, however soon the customer says the garment is wanted.
